title: Senior's toolkit: Docker Compose
summary: The compose commands for starting a stack, waiting for health, reading one service's logs and running one-off tasks.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: Docker Compose
steps.body: Compose v2 is `docker compose` (a space, not a dash). These are the commands for running a whole stack on a laptop or a CI runner.

toolkit.what: Builds what changed, starts the stack in the background and returns only when every service is running and healthy.
flags: block until healthchecks pass (implies `-d`); fails if one does not
toolkit.example: docker compose up -d --wait --build && dotnet test tests/Api.IntegrationTests
toolkit.when: before integration tests, locally and in CI

toolkit.what: Logs of one service (or several), without the noise of the rest of the stack.
flags: drop the `api-1 |` prefix, for piping to jq

toolkit.what: Every service, its state, health and ports. `-a` also shows the ones that exited.
A shell (or any command) inside a running service, addressed by service name.
flags: no terminal, for scripts and CI
toolkit.example: docker compose exec db psql -U app -d shop -c 'select count(*) from orders;'

toolkit.what: A one-off container from a service's definition: migrations, seed scripts, a REPL. It gets the same network, env and volumes.
flags: do not start the services it depends on
toolkit.example: docker compose run --rm api dotnet Api.dll migrate

toolkit.what: Prints the final model after merging files, `.env` and variable substitution. Shows what Compose will really do.
toolkit.when: a variable or override does not seem to apply

toolkit.what: Stops and removes the stack's containers and network. Volumes stay unless you ask.
flags: remove containers of services no longer in the file

toolkit.what: Syncs source changes into running containers or rebuilds them, from the `develop.watch` section of the file.
flags: copy changed files into the container
rebuild the image when, say, the .csproj changes
on any command: include services of that profile

steps.prompt: CI runs `docker compose up -d` and then the integration tests. About one run in five fails with `Npgsql: Connection refused`. What is the fix?
options: Give `db` a healthcheck, make `api` depend on it with `condition: service_healthy`, and use `docker compose up -d --wait`
Retry the whole CI job automatically
steps.explain: `up -d` returns when containers start, not when Postgres accepts connections. A healthcheck plus `--wait` makes readiness explicit; a sleep is either too slow or still too short.

steps.prompt: Match each task to the command.
pairs: open psql in the running db
see the merged file with variables filled in
read only the api's recent logs
start and block until everything is healthy

steps.prompt: Rebuild and start the stack, returning only once every healthcheck passes.
steps.explain: `up` creates and starts; `start` only restarts existing containers. `--wait` blocks on health, `--build` rebuilds images first.

steps.prompt: A teammate says "just run `docker compose down -v` to reset". What does `-v` do that plain `down` does not?
options: Deletes the named volumes too, so the database data is gone
steps.explain: On `down`, `-v` means volumes. Great for a clean test run, terrible on a box whose data you wanted. Plain `down` keeps volumes.

steps.prompt: Keeps your data, or deletes it?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Use `up -d --wait` instead of sleeps in every script and pipeline, and read one service at a time with `logs -f --since`. When Compose seems to ignore a setting, run `docker compose config` before you edit anything.
